Section 1 of 11

Who Is the Real Jesus?

Many people recognize the name Jesus, but they have very different ideas about Him.

Some see Him only in paintings, church buildings, or religious ceremonies. Others connect His name with people who tried to control, shame, or change Native communities.

But who is Jesus according to the Bible?

Was He simply a teacher? Was He a prophet? Was He a good man whose message was later changed? Or is He someone much greater?

You deserve the opportunity to meet Jesus through His own words and actions.

Jesus Does Not Belong to One Race

Jesus was not European or American. He was born into a Jewish family in the Middle East. He lived in a land controlled by the Roman Empire.

He understood what it meant to live among people whose freedom was limited by a powerful government. He saw poverty, prejudice, political tension, religious control, and the pain of families trying to survive.

Jesus did not build His influence through money, government power, or force. He walked from community to community, teaching people, healing the sick, feeding the hungry, and restoring dignity to those who had been rejected.

His invitation was never “Change your race or culture.”

His invitation was “Follow Me.”

People have sometimes misused His name to justify cruelty. Their actions do not change who Jesus is. The best way to understand Him is to examine His life and teachings for yourself.

Jesus Existed Before His Birth

Read John 1:1–3 ↗ and John 1:14 ↗.

Jesus’ life did not begin when He was born in Bethlehem. John calls Him “the Word” and says that He was with God in the beginning. Everything that was created was made through Him.

Jesus is the Creator who entered His own creation.

Read Colossians 1:15–17 ↗.

This passage says that everything in heaven and on earth was created through Jesus. He existed before all created things, and He holds creation together.

The hands that later touched people with healing were the hands that formed humanity.

The voice that calmed storms was the voice of the Creator.

The One who gave you life came into this world so you could know Him.

Jesus Shows Us the Creator’s Heart

Some people imagine God as distant, angry, or waiting for them to fail. Jesus came to show us what God is truly like.

Read John 14:8–9 ↗.

Jesus told His followers that anyone who had seen Him had seen the Father. This does not mean Jesus and the Father are the same person. It means Jesus perfectly reveals the Father’s character.

Look at how Jesus treated people.

Read Mark 1:40–42 ↗.

A man with leprosy approached Jesus. Because his disease made him socially unacceptable, people avoided touching him. Jesus reached out and touched him before healing him.

Jesus was not afraid of someone others had rejected.

Read John 8:1–11 ↗.

Religious leaders brought a woman to Jesus and publicly exposed her sin. They wanted to use her suffering to trap Him. Jesus protected her from their cruelty, forgave her, and invited her into a different life.

He gave her both mercy and truth.

Read Mark 10:13–16 ↗.

When others treated children as interruptions, Jesus welcomed them and blessed them.

Again and again, Jesus moved toward people who felt overlooked, ashamed, or unwanted.

That is the heart of the Creator.

Jesus Understands Human Pain

Jesus did not watch human suffering from a safe distance. He entered it.

Read Isaiah 53:3–5 ↗ and Hebrews 4:15 ↗.

Jesus experienced hunger, exhaustion, grief, rejection, betrayal, injustice, and physical pain. One of His friends betrayed Him. Others abandoned Him when He needed them. Religious and political leaders worked together to condemn Him.

Jesus understands what it feels like to be misunderstood.

He understands grief that is difficult to explain.

He understands what happens when powerful people misuse authority.

He understands the pain carried by individuals, families, and communities.

You can speak honestly with Him because He already knows what pain feels like.

Why Did Jesus Die?

The Creator made humanity for life, love, and relationship. Sin brought separation, suffering, and death into that relationship.

Every person has sinned. None of us can repair that separation by being good enough, religious enough, or strong enough.

Read Romans 3:23 ↗ and Romans 6:23 ↗.

Sin leads to death. Jesus chose to take that consequence upon Himself.

Read John 3:16–17 ↗ and 1 Peter 2:24 ↗.

Jesus was innocent, yet He willingly gave His life for us. On the cross, He carried our guilt and accepted the death that sin brings.

He was not forced to do this.

Read John 10:17–18 ↗.

Jesus gave Himself because He loves us. His death shows both the seriousness of sin and the depth of the Creator’s love.

You cannot earn that love. You can receive it.

Death Did Not Defeat Him

Jesus was buried, but the grave could not hold Him.

Read Luke 24:1–8 ↗ and 1 Corinthians 15:20–22 ↗.

On the third day, Jesus rose from the dead. His resurrection was a real victory over sin and death.

Because Jesus lives, your failures do not have to define your future. Addiction does not have to speak the final word. Shame does not have to own your identity. Even death will not last forever.

Jesus offers a new life now and the promise of eternal life when He returns.

Read John 14:1–3 ↗.

Jesus promised that He would come again. His plan is to bring His people home and restore what sin has broken.

Jesus Calls You His Friend

Jesus is the Creator, but He does not ask you to approach Him as if you are worthless.

Read John 15:13–15 ↗.

Jesus called His followers friends.

A real friend listens, tells the truth, remains present during pain, and wants what is good for you. Jesus does all of this perfectly.

He knows the parts of your story that no one else sees. He knows your strongest moments, private fears, unanswered questions, and deepest regrets.

He knows everything about you and still invites you closer.

You do not have to clean up your entire life before speaking to Him. You can come as you are and allow Him to begin changing your heart.

Will Following Jesus Erase Your Identity?

Following Jesus changes every person, but it does not turn people into copies of another race or culture.

Read Revelation 7:9–10 ↗.

John saw a future gathering before God that included every nation, tribe, people, and language. Their differences had not disappeared. They were united in worship while still being recognized as people from distinct communities.

Jesus does not erase people. He brings people together.

His teachings examine every human heart and every culture. He calls all people away from hatred, pride, dishonesty, abuse, revenge, greed, and anything else that harms our relationship with the Creator or one another.

That same truth also examines institutions that have used religion to dominate others.

Following Jesus means allowing Him to lead your life. It does not require you to reject your family, despise your ancestry, or feel ashamed of being Native.

What Does Jesus Offer You?

Read Matthew 11:28–30 ↗.

Jesus offers rest to people who are tired and carrying heavy burdens.

Read John 8:36 ↗.

He offers freedom from the power of sin.

Read John 10:10 ↗.

He offers a full and meaningful life.

Read John 15:11 ↗.

He offers a joy that circumstances cannot easily destroy.

Read Hebrews 7:25 ↗.

He is alive today and represents us before the Father. You are not alone when you pray.

Jesus offers forgiveness, freedom, friendship, direction, and hope.

How Can You Begin Knowing Him?

A relationship with Jesus begins with trust.

You do not earn His acceptance through ceremonies, money, good behavior, or religious performance.

Read Ephesians 2:8–10 ↗.

You are saved by God’s grace through faith. Good actions do not purchase salvation. They grow from a life that has received His love.

You can begin by speaking honestly:

“Jesus, I want to know who You really are. Help me understand Your words. Show me what is true. Teach me how to trust You.”

Then spend time reading about His life. Pay attention to what He said, how He treated people, and what He asks of those who follow Him.

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. What ideas or images have shaped the way you see Jesus?
  2. How is the Jesus described in the Bible different from the way people have sometimes represented Him?
  3. Which action of Jesus in this lesson showed you the most about His character?
  4. What burden would you like to bring to Jesus?
  5. What part of trusting Him feels easy? What part feels difficult?
  6. If you could speak with Jesus face to face today, what would you ask Him?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside ten quiet minutes on three different days.

Read one passage each time:

  • Day 1: Mark 2:1–17 ↗
  • Day 2: John 4:4–30 ↗
  • Day 3: Luke 23:32–24:8 ↗

After each reading, write down:

  • What did Jesus do?
  • What does this show me about His character?
  • How did He treat people?
  • What might He be inviting me to believe or do?

Speak to Jesus about whatever you discover. You do not need special words. Honesty is enough.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Jesus, I want to know You as You truly are. Help me see beyond the ways Your name has been misused. Thank You for creating me, entering our suffering, and giving Your life for me. Show me what Your death and resurrection mean for my life. Help me trust Your love, hear Your truth, and walk with You one step at a time. Amen.

Remember This

Jesus is your Creator.

He entered the human family and understands pain.

He reveals the true heart of the Father.

He gave His life to free you from sin.

He rose from the dead and is alive today.

He invites you to know Him as your Savior and Friend.

Following Him does not require you to become less Native.
